To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the actuator-induced body force increases with increasing exposed electrode width, decreasing dielectric thickness, decreasing dielectric constant, decreasing applied frequency, and decreasing applied voltage amplitude.

the use of thick dielectric material with low dielectric constant and operation of the actuators at higher voltage and frequency can increase the body force by an order of magnitude compared to the results of previous studies.
actuators constructed from thick dielectric material with low dielectric constant and low conductivity are more effective at producing body force at high Reynolds number.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of dielectric barrier discharge actuators that are capable of generating body forces large enough to control the boundary layer flow on the surface of a high speed air vehicle at Reynolds numbers of interest for practical flight applications.
the development of a plasma-based flow control system that will enable the active control of aerodynamic forces on a wide range of vehicles, including aircraft and spacecraft.

developing a better understanding of plasma actuator operation and the factors that influence the magnitude of the body force produced, with the ultimate goal of improving the performance of these devices in aerodynamic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of thick dielectric materials of low dielectric permittivity in the fabrication of plasma actuators is highly recommended.

the body force generated by a single plasma actuator is proportional to the applied voltage amplitude, the exposed electrode length, and the covered electrode width and is inversely proportional to the applied frequency.

the use of a thick dielectric material in a plasma actuator can increase its thrust by an order of magnitude, and that this increase is not accompanied by an increase in the power required to produce the body force.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of thick dielectric material is a key factor in the design of high performance plasma actuators.
a dielectric barrier discharge actuator with a thick dielectric material and high applied voltages is capable of generating a larger body force than the conventional actuator.
the actuator design that provides the best performance is the one that produces the largest possible body force at the highest possible applied voltage.
The main takeaway from our work is that

plasma actuators can be optimized for high body force production and high Reynolds number operation by using a combination of high dielectric constant, low dielectric loss, thick dielectric materials and high applied voltage.
the use of thicker dielectric materials with lower dielectric constants is an important step towards achieving high authority actuators that can operate at Reynolds numbers above 10^6.
the actuator design is critical to the ability to achieve large actuation forces at high Reynolds number.
